facts.heading: Exhausted as per GP suggestion
facts.content: Daniel feels exhausted, describing it as running on fumes.
facts.evidence: She said I look exhausted, and she's right, I am.

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burned out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burned out since October.

facts.heading: Work situation since October
facts.content: Daniel's company lost a big client in October.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client,

facts.heading: Increased workload since October
facts.content: Daniel ended up doing three people's jobs after the client loss.
facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Work hours are very long
facts.content: Daniel starts work at seven and continues answering messages until ten at night.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night.

facts.heading: Sleep duration is about four hours
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about four hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours.

facts.heading: Wakes up at three AM
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: I wake up at three in the morning and can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Worry causes sleep disruption
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at three, his head starts with thoughts of shipping schedules and the client.
facts.evidence: Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current physical state
facts.content: Daniel's father's hands shake, and he is slower.
facts.evidence: His hands shake, and he's slower,

facts.heading: Daniel drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds.

facts.heading: Appointments are every few weeks
facts.content: The neurology appointments for Daniel's father are every few weeks.
facts.evidence: The neurology appointments are every few weeks,

facts.heading: Caregiving burden falls on Daniel
facts.content: Daniel is the one responsible for the care of his father because his sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls on me.

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about tiredness
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: I feel it's selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Daniel tells sister he is fine
facts.content: When his sister Hannah asks how he is, Daniel tells her he is fine.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine.

facts.heading: Daniel avoids hospital visits
facts.content: Some days, Daniel sits in the hospital car park for ten minutes before going in.
facts.evidence: some days I sit in the car park at the hospital for ten minutes before I go in, because I can't face it.

facts.heading: GP blood tests normal
facts.content: Daniel's GP ran blood tests, and they were all normal.
facts.evidence: She did blood tests, and they were all normal.

facts.heading: GP suggests talking to someone
facts.content: Daniel's GP suggested he talk to someone, but Daniel said he hadn't got time.
facts.evidence: asked if I'd thought about talking to someone. I said I hadn't got time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend booked appointment
facts.content: Claire, Daniel's girlfriend, booked the appointment.
facts.evidence: My girlfriend booked it, to be honest. Claire.

facts.heading: Girlfriend's concern for Daniel
facts.content: Claire is concerned because she feels she is done watching Daniel disappear.
facts.evidence: She said she was done watching me disappear.

facts.heading: Claire's patience with Daniel
facts.content: Claire is patient with Daniel and makes him tea without pushing him to talk.
facts.evidence: She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Claire's reduced weekend invitations
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel to go away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend

facts.heading: Daniel's reason for declining trips
facts.content: Daniel avoids trips because he anticipates returning to two hundred emails and his Dad might need something.
facts.evidence: If I'm away I'll come back to two hundred of them. And Dad might need something.

facts.heading: Last time properly off
facts.content: Daniel cannot remember the last time he was properly off.
facts.evidence: I can't remember the last time I was properly off.

facts.heading: Running habit before October
facts.content: Daniel used to run ten kilometres every Saturday morning for six years before October.
facts.evidence: I ran. Ten kilometres every Saturday morning. I'd done it for six years.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago because his legs felt like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs felt like lead,

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at eleven at night and expects answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at eleven at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Daniel answers boss's emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even if he is in bed.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm in bed.

facts.heading: Fear of being seen as uncommitted
facts.content: Daniel fears his boss will think he is not committed if he doesn't answer the emails.
facts.evidence: That he'd think I wasn't committed.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss during restructuring
facts.content: Daniel is afraid he might be let go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Mortgage responsibility
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Mood is flat and irritable
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling mostly flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Snapped at colleague last week
facts.content: Daniel snapped at a colleague last week over nothing.
facts.evidence: I snapped at a colleague last week over nothing

facts.heading: Heart symptoms in toilet
facts.content: Daniel experienced his heart racing and hands shaking in the toilet.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Panic attacks on train
facts.content: Daniel has experienced panic attacks a couple of times. One occurred on the train to Manchester, requiring him to get off and stand on the platform.
facts.evidence: A couple of times. Once on the train to Manchester. I just had to get off and stand on the platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that his symptoms mean he is losing control or not coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up like, I don't know. Not coping.

facts.heading: Caffeine intake amount
facts.content: Daniel consumes about six cups of coffee per day.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I'm on about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings, consuming two or three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine causes uneasiness
facts.content: Daniel feels uneasy about the wine, and it only works for an hour before he wakes at three.
facts.evidence: Uneasy. It works for an hour and then I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from speaking out
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after speaking about his issues, like putting down a bag.
facts.evidence: A bit of a relief, actually. Like putting down a bag I didn't realise I was carrying.

facts.heading: Primary sleep concern
facts.content: Daniel believes that if he could sleep, he could cope with the rest of his issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family history of stoicism
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather and father both worked in mines and never complained about anything.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked in the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything, not once.

facts.heading: Belief about family perception
facts.content: Daniel worries that his grandfather would think he was weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Daniel's self-perception
facts.content: Daniel states that he is not weak, but very tired.
facts.evidence: That I'm not weak. I'm just very tired.

facts.heading: Plan to limit phone use
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try turning off his phone for twenty minutes every evening.
facts.evidence: Yes. Half past nine, perhaps.

facts.heading: Plan for phone-free time
facts.content: Daniel plans to make the twenty-minute phone-free time a routine with Claire, involving tea on the sofa.
facts.evidence: I could make it a thing with Claire. Tea on the sofa.

facts.heading: Plan to track sleep
facts.content: Daniel agreed to write down how his night goes, specifically when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I'll write down when I wake up, if I wake up.

facts.heading: Daniel's attendance at next session
facts.content: Daniel plans to attend the next session.
facts.evidence: Yes. I'll be here.
